# App skeleton

Stack: React 19 + react-router-dom 6 + Vite 8 (client), Express 4 run by tsx (server), TypeScript strict, Vitest, Playwright.
All dependencies are installed. Do not add packages.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/` | Client. Entry `main.tsx` already imports `styles/tokens.css` (design tokens). |
| `server/index.ts` | Boots Express: `GET /api/health`, `POST /api/reset`, `registerRoutes(app)`, unknown `/api/*` → 404 JSON, static `dist/` + SPA fallback. Rarely needs edits. |
| `server/routes.ts` | Put every API endpoint here inside `registerRoutes(app)`. |
| `server/db.ts` | JSON-file store: `readDb<T>()` returns the whole dataset (mutate it, then `writeDb(db)`), `resetDb()` restores the seed. |
| `server/data/seed.json` | Resolved domain seed copied from `../requirements/seed.json`. The original optional input stays unchanged. `server/data/db.json` is the live copy. |
| `shared/` | Domain types and pure business/validation logic with meaningful `*.test.ts` tests when the brief needs them. No fixed entity names or pricing module is required. |
| `e2e/` | Playwright specs. |
| `visual-evidence/` | Desktop/mobile PNGs for each target in `../design/visual-plan.json`, outside `test-results/`. |

Imports between files are extensionless (`import { x } from './db'`).

## Commands (run from this directory, one plain command at a time)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | Type-check (`tsc`) then `vite build` into `dist/` |
| `npx vitest run` | Unit tests (`{src,server,shared}/**/*.test.ts(x)`); missing tests fail |
| `npx playwright test` | Builds, starts the server on port 3100, runs `e2e/`; add `--grep "<case-id>"` to run one case |
| `npm start` | Production server on `PORT` (default 3000) serving API + `dist/` — long-running, do not run it yourself |

## Verification contract

Keep one Chromium project and one worker: every test resets the same JSON store.
Call `POST /api/reset` in `beforeEach`; do not run mutation tests in parallel.
Acceptance tests belong in `e2e/case-<id>.spec.ts` with exact IDs from
`../requirements/acceptance.json`. Cases can be supplied by the brief or derived
from requested behavior when the brief has no explicit tests. Additional tests belong in
`journey.spec.ts`, `edge-cases.spec.ts`, `smoke.spec.ts`, and `visual.spec.ts`.
Do not change official expected values or hide failures with retries or skips.

Read `../requirements/product.json` for the actual roles, entities and primary
journey; anonymous and single-screen products are supported. Never introduce
an unrelated marketplace, approval flow, money formula or persona switcher.
For static presentation with no meaningful pure logic, the reviewed product may
set `unit_tests_required: false` and explain `unit_test_reason`; the runner marks
unit verification not applicable only if no existing unit files need execution.

The desktop viewport is 1440×900. Visual tests also use 390×844 via
`page.setViewportSize`, preserving one project and sequential resets. The
designer chooses 1–3 representative screens or states in `../design/visual-plan.json`.
Capture every target in both sizes as `visual-evidence/{desktop|mobile}-{target.id}.png`.
Use `page.screenshot({ path, fullPage: true, animations: 'disabled' })`, attach
the PNG with `testInfo.attach`, and wait for actual content and loaded images
before capture. Assert no horizontal page overflow. Do not use fixed sleeps.

Screenshots support a separate visual review. After polish and final regression,
the visual reviewer reads every final planned PNG and records findings in
`../quality/visual-review.json`; the runner stamps the review and screenshot
and visual-plan hashes in `../quality/evidence.json` so stale evidence cannot pass.

# Hackathon Challenge: Wheels2Go

### 1. User Roles

- **Car Owner:** Can create, edit, manage car listings, review booking requests, and track earnings.

Provide a simple way to switch between demo Owner and Renter accounts for judging purposes.

### 2. Car Owner Features

**Car Listing Management**

Owners can:

- Create new car listings.
- Edit existing listings.
- Enable or disable listing availability.
- Delete their own listings.

- Make, Model, Year
- Fuel Type (Gasoline, Hybrid, Electric)
- Transmission (Automatic, Manual)
- Number of Seats
- Daily Rental Rate
- Cleaning Fee

**Booking Management**

- View booking details and renter information.
- Track booking status.

**Earnings Dashboard**

Display:

- Total completed rentals.
- Total revenue earned.
- Number of pending requests.
- Revenue summary.

### 3. Renter Features

**Car Marketplace**

Display available cars in a responsive grid layout.

Each car card must show:

- Car image
- Make, Model, Year
- Daily rental price
- Fuel type and transmission
- Number of seats
- Pickup location
- Availability status

**Search and Filtering**

Support filtering by:

- Make / Brand
- Model
- Location keyword
- Maximum daily rental price
- Transmission type
- Fuel type

Filters must work together and update results immediately.

### 4. Booking and Pricing

Renters must be able to:

- Select a car.
- Select rental start and end dates.
- Review pickup location.
- Submit a booking request.

**Pricing Formula:**

Total Price = (Rental Days × Daily Rate) + Cleaning Fee

Display a transparent price breakdown:

- Number of rental days
- Daily rate
- Rental subtotal
- Cleaning fee
- Final total

**Booking Validation:**

- End date must be after start date.

### 5. Booking Status Lifecycle

- Pending
- Confirmed
- Cancelled
- Completed

Only the owner can approve or reject pending booking requests.

When an owner approves a booking, the updated status must immediately appear in both Owner and Renter dashboards.

Cancelled and completed bookings must be reflected consistently across the application.

- Store application data persistently using the available database or local storage.

- Changes to cars and bookings must be reflected across all relevant dashboards.

- Consistent typography, spacing, and colors.

- Clear status badges.

- Intuitive navigation.

Use the provided official seed JSON dataset containing:

- 2 demo users (1 Owner and 1 Renter).
- 3 cars (Tesla Model Y, Ford Bronco, BMW M3).
- 1 existing confirmed booking.

Preserve the original seed data and ensure it is available when the application starts.

- Location: Airport Hub.

- **Unit-testable pure logic**: days/total calculation, date validation, overlap detection, effective status, filter function, earnings aggregation, listing validation.

## 6. API and persistence contract
JSON; errors `{ "error": { "code": string, "message": string, "fields"?: {field: message} } }` with 400 (validation), 403, 404, 409. Active user passed via `X-User-Id`. Shared TypeScript types for User/Car/Booking/etc. are used by server and client.

- `GET /api/health` → `{ "ok": true }`.
- `POST /api/reset` → restores seed exactly; `{ "ok": true }`.
- `GET /api/users` → `User[]` (for the switcher).
- `GET /api/cars` → `Car[]` (all, including unavailable). Filtering is client-side or optional query params.
- `GET /api/cars/:id` → `Car` (404 if missing).
- `POST /api/cars` (owner) body: Car fields without `id`, `owner_id`, `status` → 201 `Car`; 400 with `fields`.
- `PUT /api/cars/:id` (owner of car) body: same fields plus optional `status` → `Car`.
- `PATCH /api/cars/:id/availability` (owner of car) body `{ "status": "available"|"unavailable" }` → `Car`.
- `DELETE /api/cars/:id` (owner of car) → 204; 409 if pending/confirmed bookings.
- `GET /api/bookings` → bookings scoped to the active user (renter: own; owner: on own cars), with effective status, embedded `car` and `renter`.
- `POST /api/bookings` (renter) body `{ car_id, start_date, end_date }` → 201 `Booking` (pending); 400 dates, 404 car, 409 unavailable/conflict, 403 owner.
- `PATCH /api/bookings/:id/status` body `{ "status": "confirmed"|"cancelled" }` → `Booking`. Owner of car: confirm/reject pending; renter owner of booking: cancel pending/confirmed pre-start; other → 403/409.
- `GET /api/earnings` (owner) → `{ completed_rentals, total_revenue, pending_requests, confirmed_revenue, by_car: [{car_id,title,completed_rentals,revenue}] }`.

Persistence: server-side store initialized from the resolved seed on first start; survives restarts/refresh; reset rewrites it.

## 7. Primary journey
See `product.json`. Renter filters Tesla, opens Model Y, selects 2026-12-01→12-04, sees $280.00, submits → Pending in My Bookings. Owner switches account, approves in Booking Requests → Confirmed. Renter switches back, sees Confirmed. Refresh retains everything. Both dashboards read the same API data, so no manual sync is required; switching account refetches.

## 8. UI and non-functional
- Responsive from 360px (no horizontal scroll; grid 1 column on mobile, 2–3 on larger); modern, premium look with consistent typography, spacing, and colors.
- All inputs have visible labels; all controls keyboard-operable with visible focus; buttons have text/aria-labels; status badges use text plus color (Pending amber, Confirmed green, Cancelled red/gray, Completed blue).
- Loading, empty, error, and success states (toast/inline `role="status"`) for lists and mutations. Destructive actions (delete, cancel, reject) ask for confirmation.
- Stable test hooks: `data-testid` on car cards (`car-card`), filters (`filter-make`, `filter-model`, `filter-location`, `filter-max-price`, `filter-transmission`, `filter-fuel`), `account-switcher`, price breakdown (`price-days`, `price-daily-rate`, `price-subtotal`, `price-cleaning-fee`, `price-total`), `booking-card`, `status-badge`, approve/reject buttons.
- A README with run instructions and demo accounts is required deliverable.

## 9. Resolved seed and traceability
`requirements/seed.json` = `input/seed.json` (2 users, 3 cars, 1 confirmed booking `book_301` Miami Tesla 2026-11-10→11-13, $280) with all original records and values preserved. The only addition is `pickup_instructions` on each of the 3 cars, because the brief requires this field on every listing. The seed is compatible with the brief (no mismatch). No completed booking is added, so Earnings initially shows 0 completed rentals/$0.00 revenue and $280.00 expected from confirmed (this is intentional to preserve the original dataset).

- Demo switcher is not authentication; `X-User-Id` is trusted.
